final_message:
I've written the September 2026 trends report for Bluebird Bakery Co as a draft for the reviewer. The report and its data file are in `evals/runs/v5-run-20261013/c_bb_subtotal_mismatch/skill_output/`:
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.md` — the draft report, with 8 commentary bullets in section 1 and the "DRAFT" banner kept
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.json` — the analysis data that every figure comes from

**Data quality: one mismatch the reviewer needs to settle.** "Total for Professional Services" in Mar 2026 shows 2,225.00 in the workbook, but its line items add up to 2,200.00 (a 25.00 difference). The report uses 2,200.00; which figure is right is the reviewer's call. Gross profit, net income and the balance sheet all match the workbook's own totals in every month. Two notes on how the sheet was read:
- "Total Delivery" had no heading row, so I grouped Delivery Van Fuel and Courier: Same Day under it because they add up to it every month.
- "Charitable Donations" has no figures and no total row, so it's counted as zero.

**Main points:**
- **Revenue was 81,300**, up 17.7% on August (69,050) and 17.3% above the previous six-month average (69,292). A new stream, Wholesale Accounts, accounts for 12,000 of September revenue after six months at zero. Pastry Sales have fallen by about 2% every month, and Catering Revenue dropped from 9,100 in July to 3,800.
- **Gross margin was 65.3%**, up 5.7 points on August and the highest in the nine months.
- **Operating expenses were 31,570, up 21.0%.** Almost all of the increase is Wages & Salaries, up 5,000 to 21,000; the reviewer should confirm whether this is a one-off. Mystery Shopper Program (400) is not new: it also appears in March and June.
- **Net income was 21,553**, up from 15,077, and has been positive in all nine months. Even so, cash fell to 37,600: down 1,800 on August and 10,800 on six months earlier.

There are no year-over-year or trailing-twelve-month comparisons, because the export only covers nine months (Jan–Sep 2026). The commentary says so.

Three expense accounts didn't match any category and are grouped under "Other Opex": Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates (a credit of 250 in September). The reviewer may want to add categories for them in `category_map.json`.

The output folder is inside an eval run directory, so if `run_evals.py` is running against it, the reviewer should check that nothing else is writing there before treating these as the case's output.
